artworks.title: Apprehension
artworks.medium: charcoal and chalk on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Mrs. Arthur B. Davies, wife of the artist, 1930)
artworks.description: The image shows a full-body drawing of a person in a crouched, forward-leaning position, reaching out with one arm extended forward and the other bent slightly back. The subject's facial features are in profile, with softly drawn details and shading emphasizing the expression. The hair is styled up, with textured strands. The drawing is a nude study, showcasing the natural curves and musculature of the body in detailed sketching. The person is barefoot with both feet planted firmly. The background is a plain, blank brown paper.

artworks.title: Lord Camden
artworks.medium: engraving
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Bequest of Frank B. Bristow, 1968)
artworks.description: The image shows a person standing in a poised manner with their right hand rested on a large book atop a table, and their left hand partly raised in front of their chest. The person has long, voluminous, curly white hair and is dressed in an elaborate period robe with fur-trimmed sleeves and a decorative collar. They wear a beaded chain or necklace, and the table holds a quill in an inkstand and several books. To the left, there's an ornate chair with detailed carvings. In the background, there is a grand column and a heavy draped fabric, creating a stately interior environment with a cloudy sky visible through an opening.

artworks.title: Two Views of a Dancing Nude
artworks.medium: pastel on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Mrs. Arthur B. Davies, wife of the artist, 1930)
artworks.description: The image features two full-length figures drawn in a sketch-like style on a tan background. Both figures are standing facing each other. The figure on the left is shown in profile, with her right hand on her hip and her left arm extended outward, touching the other figure's right arm. She has reddish-brown hair styled up. The figure on the right is depicted from behind, with her right arm bent at the elbow and touching the other figure's left arm. Her left hand rests on her waist with similar styled hair. Both figures appear unclothed, emphasizing their form and posture. The background is a textured surface that emphasizes the figures.

artworks.title: Woman with Red and Blue Scarf
artworks.medium: pastel on gray laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Mrs. Arthur B. Davies, wife of the artist, 1930)
artworks.description: The image shows a full-body drawing of a person in a bent-over position against a gray background. The figure's details are depicted using white and gray tones. The person has short, pale-colored hair and indistinct facial features. They are wearing a vibrant blue and orange scarf or cloth that falls over their shoulder and drapes to the ground.

artworks.title: After Strife
artworks.medium: charcoal and pastel on gray paper mounted to board
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Mrs. Arthur B. Davies, wife of the artist, 1930)
artworks.description: The image displays curving lines and rounded forms creating an abstract depiction of human figures on a textured background. The shapes evoke the appearance of intertwined bodies bending and stretching. The figures are positioned horizontally, bending downwards, with lines suggesting movement and interaction. The human forms are accentuated by subtle variation in tones and shading, enhancing their muscular definition and dynamic poses.

artworks.title: The Green Dress
artworks.medium: pastel on wove paper mounted to composition board
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Bequest of James Parmelee, 1941)
artworks.description: The image shows a seated woman, partially turned to her right. Her facial features are softly defined and her hair is styled back. She wears an off-shoulder gown in light tones with green and blue accents, blending into a brown background.

artworks.title: Commodore John Barry
artworks.medium: graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, Membership Association Fund, 1951)
artworks.description: This image depicts a pencil sketch of a man from the waist up. The man has an oval-shaped face with prominent facial features, including a straight nose and defined cheekbones. His eyes are focused and his expression is neutral. He has wavy, short hair and is wearing a high-collared jacket or coat with buttons down the front, typical of early 19th-century fashion. The sketch is simple with minimal shading and a plain background. The artist's signature and the year 1830 are visible near the lower right corner.

artworks.title: The Bride of Lammermoor
artworks.medium: pen and black ink, wash, and graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of J. William Middendorf, II, 1977)
artworks.description: The image depicts two full-body figures positioned closely together outdoors. The man is standing on the left, slightly bent towards the woman who is seated on a stone structure. He has distinctive facial features with a prominent nose and a slight mustache, wearing a wide-brimmed hat with a feather, an elaborate coat over a suit, and boots. The woman wears a voluminous dress and has long, wavy hair. They are in front of an aged stone archway covered in vines, surrounded by trees and scattered shrubbery and stones.

artworks.title: Barking Dog and Studies for "Militia Training"
artworks.medium: graphite and ink wash on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of J. William Middendorf, II, 1977)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of small vignettes on a single sheet. The drawing depicts various sketches scattered across a pale background. There is a darkly shaded dog in the lower right corner in a dynamic pose. Surrounding this are faint sketches of human figures in different compositions, including several gesturing or interacting with each other. These include a small group pointing, a duo engaged in an activity on the upper left, and several other figures positioned around the page. The drawing is executed with a minimal, loose line style, indicating quick, observational sketches capturing movements and interactions.

artworks.title: Inlaid Chamber, Sizerch, Westmorland
artworks.medium: hand-colored lithograph on wove paper mounted to board
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Mrs. Benjamin Ogle Tayloe, 1879)
artworks.description: This is an image of an opulent, historic interior room. The scene features a richly decorated room with a grand four-poster bed, elaborate wood carvings, red curtains, intricate wood paneling, and decorative details. There is a plush red carpet, a desk with a chair, a tall window, and a table with decorative items. The room exudes grandeur and elegance in the style of Ludwig Grünwald.

artworks.title: Ponte Vecchio, Florence
artworks.medium: etching in brown on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, Mary E. Maxwell Fund, 1927)
artworks.description: The image depicts a historic bridge surrounded by old buildings. The viewpoint focuses on the buildings and their details, extending upwards and obscuring the horizon. The structures on the bridge show windows and balconies, typical of urban architecture. The brushstrokes are etched, providing texture and depth, particularly in the stonework and water reflections. The color palette is sepia, creating a vintage feel. The water under the bridge reflects the architecture above, with a small boat on the right side.

artworks.title: The Indian Bear Hunter
artworks.medium: gouache and watercolor on wove paper mounted to paperboard
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Mr. and Mrs. Hamilton Robinson, 1978)
artworks.description: The image shows a person crouched beside a large, snow-covered rock in a forest. The person has a serious expression and distinct features, including high cheekbones, a straight nose, and long dark hair tied with red ribbons. They are wearing a fur hat, a long brown coat, and holding a rifle. Rings or hoop earrings are visible on their ears. The environment is snowy, with tall, bare trees, and a bear walking in the snow to the right. The sky has a warm, yellow-orange hue.

artworks.title: Head of an Old Man (Tête de vieillard)
artworks.medium: etching [aquatint?]
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of E. Gerald Lamboley, 1993)
artworks.description: The image shows an etching of a man's upper body, including his head and shoulders. The man is depicted in a three-quarter view with his head slightly turned to his left. His facial features are detailed, with prominent eyebrows, a long nose, and a full beard that covers most of his lower face. His hair is sparse, receding, and blends into his beard. The man's attire appears to be a jacket or coat with a visible collar, and there's a textured suggestion of a shirt underneath. The background of the image is filled with dense, parallel diagonal lines.

artworks.title: Study for "View of Springfield on the Connecticut River"
artworks.medium: graphite with gray wash on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, Membership Association Fund, 1948)
artworks.description: The image shows a landscape with buildings, water, hills, and trees. The viewpoint is elevated, providing a wide view of the scene. Various details such as trees, buildings, and the water are depicted with different brushstrokes. The color scheme is mostly muted, with shades of gray and sepia dominating the image. The foreground includes grass, rocks, and trees, leading towards buildings and a large body of water. In the distance, hills, trees, and structures can be seen against the horizon.

artworks.title: A Conjugal Difference
artworks.medium: watercolor and gouache on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Mr. and Mrs. Ralph E. Becker, 1961)
artworks.description: The image depicts two individuals within a wooden cabin-like room with no windows. The person on the left is sitting on the floor against a wall, with only the upper half of their body visible. The person on the right is standing with their back slightly to the viewer, displaying their full height, and they are bent slightly forward towards the sitting person. The floor is wooden, with several objects scattered around, including a tipped-over chair, a jug, and a metal bowl on the floor. A coat or jacket is hanging on the wall behind the seated person. The walls are made of horizontal wooden planks.

artworks.title: Ai Telled Him to Stan Off
artworks.medium: pen and black ink on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum exchange, 1960)
artworks.description: The image shows two individuals in a rustic interior setting. The woman on the left is standing facing the man, holding a large knife. She has long hair tied back or under a bonnet, and is dressed in a long-sleeved dress. The man on the right is standing facing the woman, holding a rifle. He has facial hair and long hair, and is dressed in a tunic-style top with a sash or belt, pants, and moccasin-style shoes. He carries a powder horn over his shoulder. Behind them, a child is seated at a spinning wheel, observing the scene. The room features a large fireplace with a mantle holding various items. There's a stool near the man, and the walls and floor are made of wood.

artworks.title: Study for "Christ Appearing to Mary"
artworks.medium: graphite on tracing paper mounted to board
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, Membership Association Fund, 1951)
artworks.description: The image shows two figures. One is a crouching figure in profile, kneeling with their hands extended forward. They wear flowing robes and have no visible facial features. The second figure stands upright on the right side, also wearing draped clothing and facing away with unclear facial features. The background is plain, highlighting the interaction between the figures. The artwork is sketched with soft, linear techniques on a parchment-like background.

artworks.title: Shag Rocks, Nahant, Massachusetts
artworks.medium: graphite and gray wash on wove paper laid down to board
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Mrs. Roger H. Plowden, daughter of the artist, 1954)
artworks.description: The image shows a coastal scene with rugged rocks leading to the sea. Near the viewer are large rock formations with defined cracks and textures. Brushstrokes create a soft look for the rocks and distant landscape. Sailboats are seen on the water against a pale sky. Less detailed rocks in the distance add depth. The color palette is subdued, with grayscale tones and hints of muted green highlighting the natural elements.

artworks.title: House by a Pond
artworks.medium: lithograph in black on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, Mary E. Maxwell Fund, 1952)
artworks.description: The image shows a stone house set in a landscape. The house has tall windows, chimneys, and a dark, sloping roof. Surrounding trees partially obscure the horizon. The scene is depicted in a classic etching style, using fine, linear brushstrokes to define textures. The color palette is primarily brown and beige, giving the image an antique appearance. A body of water in front of the house reflects its image, with gently rippling water suggesting a tranquil setting. Dense trees in the background create a green backdrop.

artworks.title: Studies of Men
artworks.medium: graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of the Old Print Shop, 1949)
artworks.description: The image displays a series of pencil sketches of a person in various poses on a faded beige paper. One sketch shows a person standing with arms crossed, another shows the person seated or crouched with arms raised, and a third depicts the person swinging an object. The facial features are simplistic with short hair, and the clothing appears to be a shirt and pants. The background is plain.

artworks.title: Man Seated in Hitchcock Chair
artworks.medium: watercolor and graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Mrs. Josephine Boardman Crane, 1955)
artworks.description: The image depicts a person seated in profile view. The individual is sitting sideways on a wooden chair with their legs crossed at the ankles and arms folded across their chest. Their head is slightly tilted upward, showing a clean-shaven face with distinct features and a contemplative expression. The person has medium-length hair combed back from the forehead. They wear a long, textured coat, light-colored pants, and dark shoes. There are no visible jewelry or objects being held. The background is simple and unadorned, with a soft, neutral tone.

artworks.title: Studies of Women by the Park Railing
artworks.medium: charcoal on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum exchange through a gift of Mrs. William J. Glackens, wife of the artist, 1948)
artworks.description: Three sketches of women are shown, each standing in different positions. The first woman stands on the left with her hands on her hips. She wears a brimmed hat and a long dress. The second woman is in the center, leaning forward with her hands on a railing. She wears a long-sleeved dress and a hat with a broad rim. The third woman on the right is walking away with an object in her left hand. She has her hair styled up and is wearing a long dress. The background is a simple, plain surface, likely the deck of a ship.

artworks.title: In a French Village
artworks.medium: pastel on gray wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Mrs. Armistead Peter III [Caroline Ogden-Jones Peter], 1964)
artworks.description: The image shows a pastoral scene with a building featuring distinct architecture as the central focus. The style is impressionistic with soft, sketch-like brushstrokes and a color palette of muted earthy tones. A tree with budding greenery leans slightly in the foreground, and other rooftops and shrubbery are visible in the distance.

artworks.title: Village Street
artworks.medium: pastel on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Mrs. Armistead Peter III [Caroline Ogden-Jones Peter], 1964)
artworks.description: The image shows a scene from an elevated point looking down, with a house and dense foliage obscuring the horizon. The house is towards the left, and its rooflines create horizontal lines amidst the vertical and diagonal lines of the trees. The brushstrokes suggest movement, especially in the branches and foliage, with colors like blue, orange, and brown. The color palette includes earthy tones and cooler blues. The lower part has rich detail with a path leading to the house and dense tree branches, while the distance shows softer outlines of the natural surroundings extending beyond.
